_readme: Everything the inner voice says. Writers can change any sentence. Keep the key names (left of the colons). Words in {curly braces} are filled in by the game: {value} = the player's total, {limit} = the mission limit, {unit} = the unit.

setup._readme: What the inner voice says after each setup answer. {name} = the name the player typed. It is never wrong: it only knows what the player's character knows (easy = the scientist, an expert; medium = the janitor, an everyday adult; hard = the student, a kid).
setup.name: {name}. Okay. That's my name. Please don't forget it, brain.

mars_orbit.easy: Mars orbit. We circle the planet and map it from above. Our crew rides along on this trip, so I should really learn which button is the brakes.
mars_orbit.medium: Mars. The red one. We go around it, not onto it. I think that's the safer way?
mars_orbit.hard: Mars! Like in the movies! But we only go around it. Okay. Still cool.

jezero_crater.easy: Jezero Crater. A dried-up river delta, which is where water once left clues about life. The ground is rough, so the landing needs a steady thumb.
jezero_crater.medium: Jezero. An old river delta, they say. We land ON Mars this time? On the actual ground? Okay. Okay.
jezero_crater.hard: Jezero Crater! We get to land on Mars! The ground is rough, though. I will be very careful. Very, very careful.

gale_crater.easy: Gale Crater. It is low ground, so there is more air to slow us down, which helps the landing. A tall layered mountain sits in the middle.
gale_crater.medium: Gale. It is low, so there is more air to catch us when we fall. That sounds good? I like air.
gale_crater.hard: Gale Crater! It is a big hole with a mountain in it! And the air is thick, so landing should be a little easier. I hope.

arcadia_planitia.easy: Arcadia Planitia. Ice hides under the soil here. Ice means water and oxygen for the crew, but it is cold, and cold is hard on the ship.
arcadia_planitia.medium: Arcadia. Ice under the dirt. So we can have water! And it is cold. I forgot my jacket.
arcadia_planitia.hard: Arcadia Planitia! Ice under the ground! That is so cool. Get it? Cold? Okay, I will stop.

europa_flyby.easy: Europa, a moon of Jupiter. Nobody rides along, so we need no crew supplies. The sunlight is weak, the radiation is strong and the radio signal is slow.
europa_flyby.medium: Europa. Far, far away. No crew, so nobody can be hungry. But the Sun is so weak out there. Will we have enough power?
europa_flyby.hard: Europa! A moon with a secret ocean! No crew, so only the robot goes. And the radio takes so long that I will have to plan ahead.

mars_ice.easy: Mapping the ice under the surface. Three rules: enough data, a long enough life, and a strong enough signal home. Clear.
mars_ice.medium: We look for ice, so future astronauts have water. And there are three rules to pass. I'll try to remember them.
mars_ice.hard: Ice on Mars? There's ice on Mars? Cool. Three rules. I'll write them on my hand.

small.easy: The small rocket. Cheaper, but the launch moments are tighter. A fair trade if I stay sharp.
small.medium: Small rocket. Cheaper, I think. Probably harder to launch, too.
small.hard: A small rocket. Like a bottle rocket, but bigger. Cheap. Gulp.

medium.easy: The medium rocket. A fair price and fair timing. Balanced.
medium.medium: Medium rocket. Not too big, not too small. Like porridge.
medium.hard: The middle one. Middle is the safe pick, right?

large.easy: The large rocket costs more, but its launch windows are looser. The forgiving option.
large.medium: Big rocket. Big price. Fewer scary moments, I hope.
large.hard: The big one! It costs more, but bigger has to be easier. Right?

character.scientist: Right. I'm the scientist. I actually know this stuff. Please let me remember it under pressure.
character.janitor: I'm the janitor. I know where every mop is. I don't know where Mars is. Okay, I do, it's up there.
character.student: I'm a student. I have homework due tomorrow, and now a spacecraft. Great.

review.all_good: Huh. Everything is inside the limits. Did I... do that right?
review.some_over: Something is in the red. The general is going to ask about that.

budget.what: Budget: we spent {value} {unit}. The limit is {limit}.
budget.why: NASA can't pay for a mission that costs more than its budget. It gets cancelled before launch.
budget.fix: Pick cheaper parts. The high resolution camera and the large solar panel cost the most.

mass.what: Mass: the spacecraft weighs {value} {unit}. The limit is {limit}.
mass.why: The rocket can only lift so much. Too heavy, and we never leave Earth.
mass.fix: Swap a big part for a smaller one.

power.what: Power: we have {value} {unit}. We need at least {limit}.
power.why: The parts use more power than the solar panel makes. Things start shutting down.
power.fix: Use a bigger solar panel, or parts that use less power.

communications.what: Communications: the antenna sends {value} {unit}. We need at least {limit}.
communications.why: Mars gets far from Earth. A small antenna is too slow to send our pictures.

data.what: Data: the camera collects {value} {unit}. We need at least {limit}.
data.why: Not enough pictures to make a useful ice map.

mission_lifetime.what: Mission lifetime: the spacecraft lasts {value} {unit}. We need at least {limit}.
mission_lifetime.why: The spacecraft wears out before the map is finished.
mission_lifetime.fix: A bigger solar panel keeps the batteries healthy longer.

data_live.what: Data: by the end we had {value} {unit}. We needed at least {limit}.
data_live.why: The camera was turned off, so the data stopped coming in. The ice map has holes in it.
data_live.fix: Leave the camera on: it uses too little power to help in the shadow. The basic camera has no spare data. Watch the Data row on your wrist.

communications_live.what: Communications: at the end we had {value} {unit}. We needed at least {limit}.
communications_live.why: The antenna was switched off, so no messages reached Earth.
communications_live.fix: Switch the antenna back on at the power panel as soon as there is enough power. Watch the Communications row on your wrist.

mission_lifetime_live.what: Mission lifetime: at the end we had {value} {unit}. We needed at least {limit}.
mission_lifetime_live.why: The heater was off too long. The cold wore out the parts, and the mission got shorter.
mission_lifetime_live.fix: Switch the heater back on as soon as we're out of the shadow. Every second it is off takes months off the mission lifetime.

power_event.title: Power alarm
power_event.what: Power: the batteries ran out during the mission.
power_event.why: We flew into Mars' shadow. The solar panels got no sun, the batteries couldn't run everything, and power stayed in the red.
power_event.fix: When the alarm sounds, go to the power panel and switch off the heater or the antenna. The camera uses too little to help. Real NASA teams turn the heaters down before every shadow.

food_empty.title: Food ran out
food_empty.what: Food: the crew ran out of food.
food_empty.why: The crew eats every day, about 1.8 kg of food and packaging each. The food store emptied before the trip was over.
food_empty.fix: Go to the Food station in Life Support and press E to start rationing early. Rationing makes the food last longer.

water_empty.title: Water ran out
water_empty.what: Water: the crew ran out of water.
water_empty.why: The crew drinks every day, and a leak pours water out fast if nobody stops it.
water_empty.fix: When the voice warns about a leak, run to the Water station in Life Support and press E to stop it.

air_empty.title: Air ran out
air_empty.what: Air: the crew ran out of air to breathe.
air_empty.why: Breathing uses up the air every day. The oxygen generator makes more oxygen, and nobody ran it in time.
air_empty.fix: Go to the Air station in Life Support and press E to run the oxygen generator. Press E again when the ring closes on the target.

food_low.title: Food too low
food_low.what: Food: the store was almost empty at the end.
food_low.why: The crew eats every day, and the food was not rationed, so it ran too low.
food_low.fix: Go to the Food station in Life Support and press E to start rationing. Rationing makes the food last longer.

water_low.title: Water too low
water_low.what: Water: the tank was almost empty at the end.
water_low.why: The crew drinks every day. A leak that is fixed late loses a lot of water.
water_low.fix: When the voice warns about a leak, run to the Water station in Life Support and press E at once.

air_low.title: Air too low
air_low.what: Air: the air was almost gone at the end.
air_low.why: Breathing uses up the air every day, and the oxygen generator was not run (or was run badly).
air_low.fix: Go to the Air station in Life Support and press E to run the oxygen generator. A press close to the target makes more oxygen.

solar_panel.small: The small solar panel. Cheap and light, but it adds no spare months, so the heater can't stay off long.
solar_panel.medium: The medium solar panel. A middle choice for power, cost, and weight.
solar_panel.large: The large solar panel. Lots of power, but heavy and costly, and in Mars' shadow it makes none.

camera.basic: The basic camera. Maps all of Mars, but with no data to spare.
camera.high_res: The high resolution camera. Super sharp, but heavy and expensive.

antenna.small: The small antenna. Light and cheap, but too slow when Mars is far.
antenna.large: The large antenna. Fast to Earth, but heavy. Same power as the small one.

walk.start: Okay. This is the ship. I start on the Bridge. Walk around the rooms. Press E to use things.
walk.alarm: Uh oh. We just flew into Mars' shadow! No sun on the solar panels, only batteries. POWER LOW! Get to the power panel and switch something off!
walk.alarm_banner: POWER LOW! Go to the power panel: {seconds}
walk.alarm_again: Too much power again! We're still in the shadow. Switch something off!
walk.alarm_fixed: It fits. Phew. But everything I switched off is costing me something. I'd better check my wrist.
walk.alarm_failed: Too late. The batteries are empty.
walk.mission_complete: That's it. Two years of mapping Mars, done. Time to report to the general.
walk.storm_ok: We're in Mars' shadow. No sun on the solar panels, but the batteries can run everything. Huh. Good planning?
walk.storm_over: Out of the shadow! The sun is back on the solar panels. I can switch everything back on at the power panel. That shadow stood for every real 40-minute shadow, sped up. The real orbiter goes through one every two hours!
walk.storm_over_all_on: Out of the shadow. The sun is back on the solar panels.

flight._readme: What the inner voice says during Flight (Stage 3). The voice is never wrong. The levels do not change these lines yet.
flight.start: We are on our way to Mars! This leg of the trip stands for {days} real days of flying, sped up so I can play it. The crew eats, drinks and breathes every day. Press Tab to look at the Crew supplies on my wrist, and visit the Life Support room.
flight.leg_end: The leg is over. Mars is getting close! Now for the work at Mars.
flight.ration_explain: This is the Food station. If we ration, the crew eats a little less every day. They get hungry, but the food lasts longer. Smart. I think.
flight.ration_on: Rations on! The food will last longer now. Everyone is a little hungry, but everyone is alive.
flight.ration_already: We are already rationing. The food is lasting longer.
flight.generator_start: This is the oxygen generator. It makes oxygen for the crew to breathe, like the real one on the Space Station. Run it! Press E when the ring closes on the target.
flight.generator_perfect: Perfect! The oxygen generator is running smoothly and making lots of oxygen. I did that. Me!
flight.generator_good: Good! The oxygen generator is running and making a good amount of oxygen.
flight.generator_miss: Missed the timing. The oxygen generator still starts, but it runs rough, so it makes less oxygen. A Miss still runs it, just not as well.
flight.generator_already: The oxygen generator is already running. That is enough for now.
flight.leak_warning: Uh oh. A pipe broke! The water tank is leaking and the water meter is falling fast. Run to the Water station in Life Support and press E to stop it!
flight.leak_fixed: Leak stopped! We lost some water, but not all of it. That is why we keep an eye on the meters.
flight.no_leak: The water pipes look fine. No leak right now.
flight.empty_food: The food is gone. Zero. The crew is very hungry, and that is a big problem.
flight.empty_water: The water tank is empty. Zero. A leak pours water out fast if nobody stops it.
flight.empty_air: The air is gone. Zero. The oxygen generator makes oxygen, and we needed it running.
flight.start_no_crew: We are on our way! This leg of the trip stands for {days} real days of flying, sped up so I can play it. Nobody rides along on this trip, so there are no crew supplies to look after.

reroute._readme: The words on the power panel (Reroute Power mini-game).
reroute.title: POWER PANEL
reroute.available_label: Power available (sun, or batteries in shadow)
reroute.fits: It fits. Power used is not more than power available.

off_costs.camera: Off: no pictures, no new data
off_costs.heater: Off: the cold wears out parts (less mission lifetime)

debrief.success_text: The ice map is coming in. The general nods. Just once. That's a lot, for the general.
debrief.success_note: All six readings stayed inside their limits. No problems to report.

dashboard_warnings._readme: What the inner voice says when a dashboard row turns yellow (warning) or red (danger) during the walk.

budget.warning: Budget is getting close to the limit.

mass.warning: Mass is getting close to the limit.
mass.danger: Too heavy! Mass is over the limit.

power.danger: Power is in the red! We're using more than we make.

communications.warning: The antenna is barely fast enough.
communications.danger: Communications are too slow! Earth can't hear us.

data.warning: Data is barely keeping up with the plan.
data.danger: Data is falling behind! We're not collecting enough.

mission_lifetime.warning: No spare months. The spacecraft will barely last.
mission_lifetime.danger: The spacecraft won't last long enough!

food.warning: The food is running low. The crew gets hungry.
food.danger: The food is almost gone! The crew is in trouble.

water.warning: The water is running low. Everyone is thirsty.
water.danger: The water is almost gone! The crew is in trouble.

air.warning: The air is getting stale. The meter is low.
air.danger: The air is almost gone! The crew can barely breathe.

launch._readme: What the inner voice says during Launch. start = when the screen opens. results = one short line per moment result (the game takes them in turn). summary_clean / summary_costs = after the last moment. The voice is never wrong. The levels do not change these lines yet.
launch.start: A rocket launch. A ring closes on a target. I press Space when they line up. Easy. Probably.

Perfect: Perfect! Right on the target. I have no idea how I did that.
Bullseye! I will pretend I planned that.
Perfect again! My thumb is a genius.
Good: Good! Close to the target. Close counts.
Not perfect, but good. Good is fine. Good is great, really.
Good enough! Our rocket is still happy.
Miss: Missed it! That will cost us something. But the mission is not over.
Too early or too late. Oops. Something got hurt, but we keep flying.
Miss. The ring has to line up with the target. Next time!

launch.summary_clean: Nothing lost at all! A perfect launch. I may have just been lucky.
launch.summary_costs: Some misses. The list shows what they cost us. But we are still flying! Next, the ship.

orbit_burn._readme: What the inner voice says at the orbit burn (Stage 4, before the walk). The voice is never wrong. The levels do not change these lines yet.
orbit_burn.start: We are at Mars! To stay here, the engine must slow us down. If I miss, we waste fuel. Press E when the ring closes on the target.

results.Perfect: Perfect burn! We slid into orbit like a pro. I was not even scared. Okay, a little.
results.Good: Good burn! We are in orbit. A little fuel wasted, maybe, but we are here.
results.Miss: Missed the timing. The engine burned too early or too late and wasted fuel. We are in orbit, but we paid for it.

orbit_burn.summary_clean: Nothing lost. Now the ship has to survive Mars' shadow.
orbit_burn.summary_costs: The burn cost us some fuel. But we are in orbit! Now the ship has to survive Mars' shadow.

science._readme: What the inner voice says during the science pass (in the Arrival walk). The voice is never wrong. The levels do not change these lines yet. {gb} = gigabits (Gb).
science.target_in_view: The target is in view! Hurry to the Science station and press E to capture it.
science.capture_perfect: Perfect picture! I stored {gb} Gb of data.
science.capture_good: Good picture! I stored {gb} Gb of data.
science.capture_miss: Blurry picture. Only {gb} Gb of good data stored. A Miss still counts a little.
science.capture_camera_off: The camera is switched off at the power panel, so I got nothing. Zero. Hmm.
science.storage_full: The storage is full. It can only hold {gb} Gb, so the rest of the picture was lost.
science.capture_window_missed: The target went out of view and I never took the picture. Oops.
science.station_in_view: The ground station is in view! Go to the Comms station and press E to send the data home.
science.downlink_perfect: Perfect link! {gb} Gb is on its way to Earth.
science.downlink_good: Good link! {gb} Gb is on its way to Earth.
science.downlink_miss: A shaky link. Only {gb} Gb got through.
science.downlink_antenna_off: The antenna is switched off at the power panel, so nothing was sent. Zero. The data is still stored.
science.nothing_to_send: There is nothing stored to send. I need a picture first!
science.downlink_window_missed: The ground station went out of view. The data stays stored, and none got home.
science.small_antenna_slow: The antenna is slow, so only part of the data fit through the link. A bigger antenna sends it faster.

landing._readme: What the inner voice says during the Landing (Stage 4, surface destinations). The voice is never wrong. The levels do not change these lines yet.
landing.start: We are going down to the surface! First the heat shield comes off, then the parachute, then the landing engine, and then touchdown. Press Space when the ring closes on the target.

Perfect: Perfect! Right on the target. I am as surprised as you are.
Bullseye! Nobody saw how nervous I was.
Perfect again! My thumb has a plan.
Good: Good! Close to the target. We are still falling the right way.
Not perfect, but good. Good is how all landings start.
Good enough! The lander is still happy.
Miss: Missed it! That will cost us something. But we are still falling, so keep going.
Too early or too late. Oops. We lost something, but the ground is coming!
Miss. The ring has to line up with the target. Next one!

landing.summary_clean: Nothing lost at all! We are standing on another world. I may cry a little.
landing.summary_costs: Some misses. The list shows what they cost us. But we are on the ground! Surface work comes next, so hold on to your hat.
